THE OVERALL TREND:
In the Interim Report we concluded that a review of the relevant economic and demographic data reveals a definite trend toward increasing suburban, commercial, and residential activity. This conclusion was based upon representations submitted by shippers, interested organizations, and governmental agencies. The Pennjerdel Corporation mitted one such representation showing that from 1940 to 1970 the seven county area surrounding Philadelphia has experienced enormous increases in population, manufacturing firms, and retail sales, whereas these variables have been generally static or declining for Philadelphia County (the exact statistics are presented in the Interim Report, Commercial Zones, 124 M.C.C. at 145). Pennjerdel also pointed out that from 1962 through the first 8 months of 1975, 360 industrial companies left Philadelphia County and relocated in Bucks, Chester, Delaware, and Montgomery Counties, Pa.
